findings.title: Direct dictionary access on `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` can raise `KeyError`
findings.body: `build_integration` (lines 376-377) only populates `integration.metadata["sender"]` when `state.get("sender")` is present (i.e. when the `Integration` was created from a GitHub installation webhook). If an `Integration` record was originally created through the pipeline before the webhook arrived, or before `sender` was recorded in metadata, and its `OrganizationIntegration` was later deleted, reinstalling it will find the active `Integration` without a `"sender"` key in `metadata` and raise an unhandled `KeyError` at `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` instead of returning the error page. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` (and filter `Integration.objects.get` by `provider=GitHubIntegrationProvider.key` on lines 478 and 494 since `external_id` is only unique per provider).

findings.title: `test_installation_not_found` fails on OAuth `state` mismatch instead of testing a 404 installation lookup
findings.body: Adding `OAuthLoginView` to the pipeline changed the deterministic `pipeline.signature` in tests from `ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05` to `9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3`. `test_installation_not_found` still passes `"state": "ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05"`, which causes `OAuthLoginView` to abort early at `request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature` with `"Invalid installation request."`. As a result, the mocked 404 on `GET /app/installations/{self.installation_id}` and the `IntegrationError("The GitHub installation could not be found.")` path in `build_integration` are never exercised. Update `state` to `9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3` and restore the assertion for `b"The GitHub installation could not be found."`.
